ELEMENT_PAIR.value: You hold yourself up by growing, so you feel strongest while something is being built and restless once it is finished.
You come alive when something you made gets seen, and most weeks you judge yourself by how much of you got out.
You build to keep rather than to show, and the things you go after slowly are usually the ones that stay yours.
You grow best with a line to grow against, and you finish more under someone else's rule than under your own plan.
You understand things by soaking in them rather than studying them, and your best decisions come after a night's sleep instead of a second search.
You learn by growing an idea rather than collecting it, so you understand late and keep it for good.
You are your own engine and your own company, so you do your best work beside an equal rather than under anyone's wing.
You show what you feel by making something solid rather than saying it, and what you build tends to outlast the moment.
Your drive goes wherever there is something hard to shape, and you finish more by picking one thing to provide for than by chasing every opening you spot.
You take a rule in quietly and keep it for years, and you would rather answer to a standard you chose than to a voice raised at you.
Your obligations are alive, people rooted in your ground, and the claims you keep pruned are what hold your hillside together.
Your mind learns by warmth: lessons only settle once something about them catches, and what moves you once instructs you forever.
Your endurance is so quiet you forget it has limits, and the day you finally feel tired is years after you first were.
You speak rarely and it lands like something forged, and the few words you release outlive whole conversations other people spent.
You act by channeling what moves, and wealth gathers wherever you set banks for a current, slow claims that irrigate for decades.
You want something to build more than something to be given, so you stay with what you made long after a gift would have bored you.
You work harder for a standard someone else set than for one of your own, and you usually go looking for one.
Because you would rather understand a thing than be quick about it, you keep only the answers you gave time to.
Your strength is the kind you make alone, so you measure yourself against your own last best rather than against anyone beside you.
You say one true thing rather than ten pleasant ones, so you say as much by staying quiet as by speaking.
You put more into what you make than you ever say about it, and what you make usually outgrows the plan.
You reach for what matters to you with care as much as with nerve, and over the years the balance you strike shapes what you get to keep.
You keep a rule best when you feel its weight rather than read it, and a demand with pressure behind it usually gets your fullest answer.
You trust what you have tested rather than what you were told, so you learn slowly and keep it for good.
Your stamina rises and falls in long swings, and you spend the low stretches on your own more often than in company.
